title: Universal Block Kinds (Layer 1 — structural core)
description: Closed, document-agnostic set of structural block kinds emitted by SemantiK for EVERY document genre. Layer 1 of the universal block-label ontology (block_kinds -> genre_profiles -> lexicons). A block ALWAYS carries exactly one layer-1 kind; a functional role (layer 2) is an OPTIONAL second label attached only when a genre profile resolves. DocLayNet-compatible: each kind declares its 1:1 (or n:1) mapping onto the 11 DocLayNet v1 classes so the public dataset can be reused for pre-training / eval.
$comment: Closed structural-kind vocabulary. Adding, removing, or renaming a kind requires schema and downstream-impact review. Converter-specific vocabularies need an explicit tested projection before claiming conformance. See docs/architecture/block-ontology.md#layers-and-semantics and docs/architecture/block-ontology.md#governance.

BlockKind.description: The closed layer-1 structural kind enum.

FurnitureSubkind.description: Discardable page-dressing subkinds carried on a `furniture` block via the `subkind` attribute. Furniture is LISTED (never silently dropped) so no unit goes missing, then dropped at render.

x-block-kinds.label: Section heading
x-block-kinds.description: A section / subsection heading. Carries a `level` attribute (int 1..6) resolved deterministically from font/geometry/outline, not from the model.
x-block-kinds.doclaynet_note: DocLayNet's `title` maps to our `title_block` (document title); every lower heading is `section-header`.

x-block-kinds.label: Body paragraph
x-block-kinds.description: Running prose. The default fallback kind — any block that clears no more specific structural predicate lands here (never dropped).
x-block-kinds.doclaynet_note: DocLayNet has no separate prose vs. code vs. quote class — all three fold into `text`.

x-block-kinds.label: List item
x-block-kinds.description: One item of an ordered / unordered / definition list. Carries optional `marker` (bullet/number/letter glyph) + `nesting` depth.
x-block-kinds.doclaynet_note: DocLayNet labels each item, not the enclosing list — matches this per-item granularity.

x-block-kinds.label: Table
x-block-kinds.description: A tabular grid (>=2 rows AND >=2 cols, or a bordered/ruled 2-row grid). The whole table is ONE block; cells are its children.

x-block-kinds.label: Figure / image
x-block-kinds.description: A raster or vector illustration, chart, diagram, or photograph. Carries an `alt` + `src` attribute; a captioner may fill alt text.

x-block-kinds.label: Chart / graph
x-block-kinds.description: A data visualization (bar/line/pie chart, plot, graph) — distinct from figure because ACCESSIBILITY requires a data description (a prose summary or data table of the encoded values), not just alt text.
x-block-kinds.doclaynet_note: No DocLayNet chart class — folds into picture (lossy, documented gap); DocLayNet ingest lands on figure, chart requires SemantiK's own signal (caption/axis-text/geometry).

x-block-kinds.label: Caption
x-block-kinds.description: A figure or table caption. Bound to its target by the `caption_of` structural relation.

x-block-kinds.label: Display math
x-block-kinds.description: A display (block-level) mathematical expression or numbered equation. Rendered to presentation-MathML with alttext.
x-block-kinds.doclaynet_note: 1:1 (DocLayNet calls it `formula`). Inline math stays inside its host paragraph and is NOT a separate block.

x-block-kinds.label: Code / preformatted
x-block-kinds.description: A preformatted source-code or verbatim block (whitespace-significant).
x-block-kinds.doclaynet_note: NO native DocLayNet class — DocLayNet folds code into `text`. This is a lossy DocLayNet mapping (documented gap): our kind is finer than DocLayNet here.

x-block-kinds.label: Block quotation
x-block-kinds.description: An extended quotation set off from body prose.
x-block-kinds.doclaynet_note: NO native DocLayNet class — folds into `text` (lossy, documented gap).

x-block-kinds.label: Aside / sidebar
x-block-kinds.description: An out-of-flow complementary block — sidebar, margin note, boxed digression, pull-out panel — set apart from the main reading flow; renders as <aside> (a11y role=complementary) and is EXCLUDED from the main reading sequence; genre profiles refine it (instructional definition_box, technical_manual safety_notice, statistical data_highlight).
x-block-kinds.doclaynet_note: No DocLayNet aside class — folds into text (lossy, documented gap).

x-block-kinds.label: Footnote / endnote
x-block-kinds.description: A foot-of-page or end-of-document note. Bound to its reference by the `footnote_of` structural relation.

x-block-kinds.label: Form field
x-block-kinds.description: An interactive / fillable form region: a label-value pair, a text entry, or a checkbox. The `forms` genre profile refines it (field_label / field_value / checkbox_item roles).
x-block-kinds.doclaynet_note: NO DocLayNet class — DocLayNet has no form vocabulary. Ours-only kind (documented gap); a form doc is DocLayNet-blind.

x-block-kinds.label: Document title
x-block-kinds.description: The document-level title (masthead / cover title), distinct from a section heading.
x-block-kinds.doclaynet_note: 1:1 with DocLayNet `title` (document-scope title). Lower headings are `section-header`.

x-block-kinds.label: Separator / rule
x-block-kinds.description: A horizontal rule, thematic break, or column/section divider carrying no text.
x-block-kinds.doclaynet_note: NO DocLayNet class (DocLayNet drops rules). Ours-only kind (documented gap).

x-block-kinds.label: Page furniture
x-block-kinds.description: Discardable page dressing — running headers, page numbers, footer notices, watermarks. LISTED so no unit is lost, then dropped at render. Carries a `subkind` attribute from FurnitureSubkind.
x-block-kinds.doclaynet_note: Subkind-dependent: running_header -> page-header; page_number / footer_notice -> page-footer; watermark -> no DocLayNet class (documented gap).

x-doclaynet-coverage.description: Inverse map: every one of DocLayNet's 11 classes has >=1 layer-1 home, so a DocLayNet-labelled page can be ingested as weak supervision.
